decisions.note: R4→5: maker guessed title from URL text; client demanded the real page title (browser-tab title).
R4→5: card showed only title/url/date; client asked for auto description and real favicon.
R4→5: clicking a saved card did nothing; client expected it to open the original url.
R5: only inline title-rename existed; client asked for a fuller edit space covering note/description/url/tags (delivered R15).
R5→6: re-saving an existing url created a second card; client rejected the duplicate-creation behaviour.

R6: of 3 offered dedup behaviours (jump-only / jump+edit / ask-each-time), client selected 'jump+edit', matching the reference's 'guide to edit existing' rule over the other two non-conforming options.
R10 (before build): client pre-emptively required tag entry to surface/reuse existing labels to avoid case-variant duplicates, ahead of the maker building label-adding.
R7: maker's 6-item settled-scope recap omitted delete entirely; client flagged its absence.
R8: search only supported plain terms; client asked for boolean NOT/OR combinations and quoted exact-phrase search.
R13: saved-copy feature converted everything to text; client required PDFs be kept/opened as real PDF files (fixed R14).
R13: snapshot feature presented with no external backstop; client asked for an Internet-Archive-style outside copy.
R15: notes were plain flat text; client asked for lightweight markdown-style formatting (bullets/bold).
R16: no import path existed at all until client, prompted by the 'hundreds of links' question, demanded bulk import of her existing bookmarks.
R16: no export path existed at all; client demanded a way to get everything back out.
R16: no sorting existed; client demanded sort-by-name/date to cope with volume.
R16: no bulk/multi-select actions existed; client demanded batch labeling/clearing scoped to the current filter.
R17: import behaviour hadn't addressed dates; client pre-emptively required original saved dates be preserved rather than stamped 'today'.
R19: bulk actions only covered add-label and flag-read-later; client required the mirror operations (bulk unlabel, bulk mark-read) that REF-BM-20 also specifies.

satisficing_miss_detail.note: R13: 'saved copy' is described only as extracted 'archived text' in a reading view, not a preserved local HTML snapshot of the page; client never questioned format fidelity, only that a copy exists.
R17/22: export produces a plain-text list of links, not the Netscape HTML bookmark format the reference specifies; client accepted it as satisfying 'don't feel trapped' without checking the format.
R17/22: import is described/used via a custom 'Title | url | Folder | date' pipe format rather than Netscape HTML; client accepted it as her real-import solution without flagging the format mismatch.

R21/22: the final 'full scope, nothing dropped' recap and client's acceptance cover search exhaustively (title/summary/notes/url, word-variation, parked booleans/quotes) but never mention `#tag` search syntax — silently absent from both the built set and the parked list.

R21/22: archive (reversible hide, distinct from permanent delete, with its own list) never surfaces anywhere in the session, built or parked; client's 'nothing quietly dropped' acceptance misses this entirely.
R21/22: bundles (saved search+tag-filter combinations) are never introduced despite being adjacent to the labels/search work covered; absent from both delivered and parked lists at final acceptance.
